nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
So most of the readers read it. It is reported from al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj: «لأقسم بيوم القيامة», taking it as the lām of the oath, with no alif in it. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a solecism according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; one only says [it] with the nūn:
لأقومن. As for the first reading, there are several views on it. Among them is that «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis, like ما مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ [al-Aʿrāf: 12]. In al-Farrāʾ's view this is wrong on two counts: first, that when «لا» is redundant one does not begin [speech] with it; and second, that «لا» is only added in a negative context, as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 511-
ما كان يرضى رسول الله فعلهما ... والطيّبان أبو بكر ولا عمر
(The Messenger of Allah would not have approved their deed, nor the two good men, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.)
i.e. Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, with «لا» redundant. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for his statement that «لا» is not added at the beginning of speech, it is as he said — there is no disagreement about it, because that would be confusing. But he has been opposed in what he said: as I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say, this view is sound — meaning the view of whoever said that «لا» is redundant. He said:
His statement that it is at the beginning of the speech does not refute this view, because the whole Qur'an has the status of a single sūra, and on this basis is its arrangement, composition and structure. It is soundly reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Qur'an all at once to the lowest heaven in the month of Ramaḍān, and then it came down piecemeal from heaven; and only the people of innovation reject this ḥadīth. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for al-Farrāʾ's statement that «لا» is only added in a negative context, he is contradicted on it. This was reported by those among the Basrans whose knowledge is trusted, among them Abū ʿUbayda, who recited: [al-Rajaz] 512- في بئر لا حور سرى وما شعر (He travelled by night into a well of perdition, and he did not perceive it.) He said: he means في بئر حور, i.e. [a well of] destruction; so he added «لا» in an affirmative context. Al-Farrāʾ disagreed with him on this and made «لا» a negation here, i.e. "in a well that yields nothing back". Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the «لا» in His saying «لا أقسم» is a rejection of their words, as you say: لا والله ما أفعل ("No! By Allah, I will not do it"); so the pause is at it [i.e. at لا], and أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ (1) is a new beginning (mustaʾnaf).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: There is no disagreement in this [verse] that the alif comes after «لا». So the view of al-Ḥasan is that «لا» is negating; and we have explained the views of others.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The reading of the Kufans is أَيَحْسَبُ; and the past is حسب, without disagreement, so the regular form in the imperfect is يحسب [with fatḥa], except that kasra has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
قادِرِينَ is in the position of naṣb (accusative), and there are several views on its accusative. Among them: it has been said that the construction is "Yes, We are able (نقدر)", and when نقدر was converted to قادرين it was put in the accusative, as al-Farazdaq said: [al-Ṭawīl] 513-
على حلفة لا أشتم الدّهر مسلما ... ولا خارجا من فيّ زور كلام
(By an oath that I will never revile a Muslim, nor will false speech go out from my mouth.)
in the sense of ولا يخرج; and when يخرج was converted to خارج it was put in the accusative. This is wrong, because each has its own inflection: you say جاءني زيد يضحك and جاءني زيد ضاحكا, and مررت برجل يضحك and برجل ضاحك. «ولا خارجا» is conjoined to the position of «لا أشتم». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the soundest thing said about it. And it has been said that the construction is: "Yes, We are capable of that, being able (قادرين)" — this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. Sībawayh said: i.e. "Yes, We will gather them, being able". Al-Farrāʾ's view is derived from this. And بنان is the plural of بنانة. Among the good things said about it is the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās: "We are able to make his fingertips a single thing, like the hoof of a camel or the hoof of a donkey, so that he would not be able to eat with them [and would eat] like the beasts; but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was bounteous to him and favoured him." And al-Ḥasan said: "We were able to make his fingers of one size, so that they would have no beauty and he could hardly benefit from them."

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: This is the lām of kay (purpose); and their calling it the lām of «إنّ» has no meaning. Rather, يريد indicates intention, i.e. his intention is to act wickedly in what lies ahead of him.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: The construction is: "at what time is the Day of Resurrection?" And the nūn of إيان «[Translator's note: so in the source, for أيّان.]» has fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t: فَإِذا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ (7) is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Shayba, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī; and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Abū Jaʿfar and Nāfiʿ read فَإِذا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ with fatḥa on the rāʾ «[Translator's note: the source prints the same vowels for both readings; the second is بَرَقَ.]». The meaning of the kasra is clear, i.e. it is bewildered and terrified by death and by the matter of the Resurrection; and برق [means] it flashed and gleamed. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ (8): its light went away.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: It may be said: الشّمس is feminine without disagreement, so why did He not say وجمعت? There are several answers to this. Among them is that the construction is "and [it was] gathered between the sun and the moon", so the masculine was construed with بين. And it has been said: since "and the sun was gathered" does not complete the sentence until one says "and the moon", and the moon is masculine, the meaning was plural, so their verb had to be masculine when placed first, as it would be when placed after. The most appropriate thing said about it is the view of al-Kisāʾī; he said: the meaning is "and the two lights, i.e. the two luminaries, were gathered"; and in another place: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الشَّمْسَ بازِغَةً قالَ هذا رَبِّي [al-Anʿām: 78]. As for Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, he says: all this is a non-real feminine, because it was not made feminine to distinguish between one thing and another, so you may treat it as masculine, since it has the meaning of "a body" and "a thing".

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
This is a maṣdar (verbal noun) without disagreement, i.e. "where is the fleeing?" Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said:
I heard Ibn ʿAbbās read أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ «[Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowels; Ibn ʿAbbās's reading is الْمَفِرُّ, with kasra.]». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a sound chain of transmission; and in the view of the Basrans it is a noun of place. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that he permits kasra in the maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: And it [الوزر] is the place of refuge. It has been said: وزير (minister) is derived from this, because the one he serves has handed his affairs over to him, so he resorts to him and relies on him. And it has been said: because the burdens (أوزار) of what the one he serves takes on are in his hand; and أوزار [also] means what consists of gold, silver and other things.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: Qatāda said: [الْمُسْتَقَرُّ means] the final end.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Among the best of what has been said about it is the statement of Qatāda; he said: of what he sent forward of obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and what he held back of His due — he will be informed of all of it. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: of what he sent forward of good or evil after him «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "what he sent forward, and what he left behind after him".]».

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
It is difficult in its i'rab and its meaning. The view of Ibn ʿAbbās is: his hearing, his sight, his hands, his feet and his limbs are witnesses against him. Abū Jaʿfar said: according to this view, الْإِنْسانُ
is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and بَصِيرَةٌ
is a second mubtadaʾ, and «على نفسه» is the khabar (predicate) of the second, and the clause is the khabar of the first. Its explanation is: "rather, man has, over himself, from himself, watchers that keep record of him and testify against him." That is one view. The view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Qatāda is that the man is himself the بصيرة (witness). Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: man, by Allah, is a witness against himself. Qatāda said: you see him, by Allah, aware of others' sins and faults, heedless of himself. According to this view «الإنسان» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and «بصيرة» is its khabar. If it is asked: why was the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] added when الإنسان is masculine? There are two answers to this. One of them is that the hāʾ is for intensiveness, as one says رجل راوية and علّامة. And it has been said: the hāʾ was added because the meaning is "rather, man is a proof (حجّة) against himself".

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: [مَعاذِيرَهُ is] a plural not according to rule in the view of Sībawayh, because the plural of عذر is not معاذير; معاذير is rather the plural of معذار.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t:
إِنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ
(17): so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guarantees its collection. For this reason the jurists declared an unbeliever whoever claims that something of it has remained [uncollected], because that is a rejection of the plain text of the revelation. Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna was asked: how were the Torah and the Gospel altered, when they are both from Allah? He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, entrusted their preservation to them — He, exalted be His praise, said: بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِنْ كِتابِ اللَّهِ [al-Māʾida: 44] — but He did not entrust the preservation of the Qur'an to anyone; He said: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ [al-Ḥijr: 9]; and what He preserves is not altered.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
The scholars differed about the meaning of this. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "So when We send it down, listen to it." Qatāda said: i.e. follow what it makes lawful and unlawful. Among the good things said about it is what Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: فَإِذا قَرَأْناهُ
— he said: He says: "So when We have made it clear" — فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ
— he said:
He says: "Then act according to what is in it."

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: Qatāda said: [it means] making clear the lawful as distinct from the unlawful. From Ibn ʿAbbās: بَيانَهُ "on your tongue".

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: I.e. the immediate state, or the immediate world.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: Because it [الْآخِرَةَ] comes after the first [world].

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: [وُجُوهٌ ... باسِرَةٌ is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: It is not permissible to put يفعل [i.e. يُفْعَلَ] in the nominative, while it was permissible in وَحَسِبُوا أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ [al-Māʾida: 71], because «لا» is a compensation [for the omitted pronoun]. And الفاقرة means the calamity, the enormous matter.

nahhas-irab:26-27.t:
كَلَّا may mean "truly" (حقا), and on this basis it would here be a beginning (mubtadaʾ) [of speech] «[Translator's note: i.e. one begins with it rather than pausing before it.]». Muḥammad ibn Jarīr claimed that the full stop here is at «كلا», and that the meaning is: the matter is not as the polytheists say, that they will not be requited for their polytheism and disobedience. إِذا بَلَغَتِ التَّراقِيَ: the governing word of إذا may be «باسرة» or «بلغت»; if the governing word is «بلغت», the apodosis is in what follows. The yāʾ was dropped from مَنْ راقٍ
because it is vowelless and the tanwīn is vowelless, and it was kept in التراقي because there is no tanwīn in it.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: [It is] in the position of the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t:
فَلا صَدَّقَ وَلا صَلَّى: لا here is a negation and not a conjunction. According to the grammarians it is not permissible to say:
ضربت زيدا لا ضربت عمرا; the reason for this is that it was disliked for the second to resemble an imprecation. In the verse, the meaning is "he did not believe and did not pray"; what indicates this is وَلكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: I.e. he went off turning away from obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disdaining the admonition; and يَتَمَطَّى is in the position of naṣb (accusative) as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:34-35.t: [أَوْلى لَكَ] is said to someone who has fallen into destruction or come close to it.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: [سُدىً is] likewise in the position of naṣb (accusative) as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that the meaning of «أن يترك سدّى» is — he says — "neglected".

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: [يُمْنى with yāʾ is] according to the masculine of المني, which is closer to it; and «تمنى» [with tāʾ] refers to the نطفة.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: I.e. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created him and fashioned him into a human being who speaks, hears and sees.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: It has been said: the meaning is "and He made of man offspring, males and females". الذكر والأنثى are a badal (substitute) from الزوجين.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: So He, Mighty and Majestic, gave a clear indication that His bringing him back to life after death is no greater than His creating him from a drop of fluid and then fashioning him into a human being until children were born to him. Al-Farrāʾ permitted عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى «[Translator's note: i.e. as يُحْيِّ.]» by transferring the vowel of the first yāʾ to the ḥāʾ and assimilating the yāʾ into the yāʾ. This is wrong according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. The reason for this — and it is the sense of what Abū Isḥāq said — is that when you say «يحيي», assimilation is not permissible by consensus of the grammarians, so that two vowelless letters do not meet; and when you say أن يحيي, assimilation is also not permissible, because the yāʾ, even though it has taken a vowel, its vowel is accidental. Moreover, how could a single letter be assimilated in a position because of a governing word that has entered upon it and is not permanent, while it may not be assimilated when it is in the position of rafʿ (nominative) — and the nominative is the basic state?

nahhas-irab:22-23.t:
وُجُوهٌ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); ناضِرَةٌ is a naʿt (adjective) of it, and ناظِرَةٌ is the khabar (predicate) of the subject. «ناضرة» may [also] be the khabar of «وجوه» and ناظِرَةٌ a second khabar; and ناضرة may be a naʿt of ناظرة or of وجوه. One also says أجوه; and it [وجوه] is the plural for many, while for few it is أوجه. On ناظِرَةٌ there are three views: one is that the meaning is "waiting"; another is that the meaning is "[looking] to the reward of its Lord"; and another is that they look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
He said: the correct one among these answers is known from the Arabic language; for that reason and others we postponed its explanation in order to mention it in the i'rab. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the view of whoever said that its meaning is "waiting", it is wrong. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: نظرت إليه [with إلى] does not mean "I waited for him"; one only says نظرته [for that]. This is the view of Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa and others whose knowledge is trusted. As for whoever said that the meaning is "to the reward of its Lord", it is also wrong according to the view of the leading grammarians, because in their view — and in the view of anyone I know — نظرت زيدا is not permissible in the sense of "I looked at his reward". We will mention the argumentation on this from the words of the imams, the scholars and the lexicographers, since it is one of the foundations of the Sunna, and we will mention what the people of whims opposed it with. We begin with the sound ḥadīths from the Messenger ﷺ, since he is the one who makes clear [what comes] from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As was read before Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb ibn ʿAlī, from Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd narrated to us: Baḥīr ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad, that Qatāda ibn Abī Umayya narrated to them from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "I have told you about the Masīḥ al-Dajjāl until I feared that you would not understand. He is short, bow-legged, curly-haired, one-eyed, his left eye effaced, neither protruding nor sunken. If you are confused about him, then know that your Lord is not one-eyed. You will not see your Lord, exalted be His praise, until you die." Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb said: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us; he said: Abū ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays al-Ashʿarī, from his father, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Two gardens of silver — their vessels and all that is in them; and two gardens of gold — their vessels and all that is in them; and nothing stands between the people and their looking at their Lord, exalted be His praise, except the cloak of grandeur over His face, in the Garden of ʿAdn." And it was read before Abū al-Qāsim ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Baghawī, from Hudba ibn Khālid, from Ḥammād ibn Salama, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā «[Translator's note: so in the source; in the known chain, Ḥammād narrates from Thābit al-Bunānī from Ibn Abī Laylā.]», from Ṣuhayb, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنى وَزِيادَةٌ [Yūnus: 26] and said: "When the people of the Garden enter the Garden and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a caller calls out: 'O people of the Garden, you have an appointment with Allah which He wishes to fulfil for you.' They say: 'What is it? Has He not made our scales heavy, whitened our faces, admitted us into the Garden and saved us from the Fire?' Then the veil is lifted for them, and they look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and nothing they have been given is dearer to them than looking at Him — and that is the 'more' (al-ziyāda)." Abū al-Qāsim said: and my grandfather narrated to me; he said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us from Ḥammād ibn Salama, with his chain, the like of it. Abū al-Qāsim said: and Hārūn ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me; he said: I heard Yazīd — meaning Ibn Hārūn — when he narrated this ḥadīth, say: whoever denies this ḥadīth is a zindīq or an unbeliever. Abū al-Qāsim said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Kūfī narrated to us, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Juʿfī, from Zāʾida: Bayān al-Bajalī narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, who said: Jarīr narrated to us; he said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said:
"You will see your Lord on the Day of Resurrection as you see this; you will not be crowded together (لا تضامون) in seeing Him" — meaning the moon. Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī said: in spite of Jahm «[Translator's note: the source has «جهيم».]» and al-Marīsī. Abū al-Qāsim said: Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-ʿAbdī and Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba narrated to us; they said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: we said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we see our Lord, exalted be His praise?" He said:
"Do you harm one another (أتضارون) in seeing the sun at midday when there is no cloud?" We said: "No." He said: "Do you harm one another in seeing the moon on the night it is full when there is no cloud?" We said: "No." He said: "Then you will not harm one another in seeing Him, just as you do not harm one another in seeing them." Abū al-Qāsim said: and I was told from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, from Yaḥyā ibn Ādam, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, who said: al-Aʿmash said: لا تضارّون means "you will not dispute with one another". Abū al-Qāsim said: and Hudba ibn Khālid narrated to us: Wuhayb ibn Khālid narrated to us: Muṣʿab ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān, from Abū Hurayra, who said: it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, will every one of us see his Lord, exalted be His mention, on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Does every one of you see the sun at midday when there is no cloud in the sky?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Does every one of you see the moon on the night it is full when there is no cloud in the sky?" They said: "Yes." He said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will see your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection; you will not harm one another in seeing Him, just as you do not harm one another in seeing them." Abū al-Qāsim said: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba narrated to us: Abū Usāma narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us: Khaythama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me, from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is none of you but his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will speak to him, with no interpreter between Him and him, and no veil screening him. He will look to his right and see nothing but what he sent forward; then he will look to his left and see nothing but what he sent forward; then he will look in front of him and see nothing but the Fire. So guard yourselves against the Fire, even with half a date." In this ḥadīth from al-Aʿmash, no one said "and no veil screening him" except Abū Usāma alone. And of that is what Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Suhayl narrated to us: Zuhayr — meaning Ibn Ḥarb — narrated to us: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Hishām al-Dastawāʾī, from Qatāda, from Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz, who said:
A man said to Ibn ʿUmar: "How did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ speak about the private conversation (al-najwā)?" He said: I heard him say: "The believer will be brought near to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, until He places His cover over him and makes him confess his sins, saying: 'Do you recognise [them]?' He says: 'My Lord, I recognise [them].' He says: 'I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' Then he will be given the record of his reckoning. As for the unbelievers and the hypocrites, they will be proclaimed before the heads of all creatures: 'These are the ones who lied against Allah.'" Abū Jaʿfar said: on this subject there are [ḥadīths] from Anas and from Abū Razīn from the Prophet ﷺ, and on it there are [reports] from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them — among them Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq and Ḥudhayfa — [and] from the Followers; but we disliked lengthiness, since the ḥadīth we have mentioned suffices. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Naysābūrī say:
The Sunna in our view — and it is the view of our imams Mālik ibn Anas, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUmar «[Translator's note: so in the source; the name appears corrupt.]», al-Awzāʿī, Sufyān ibn Saʿīd al-Thawrī, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna al-Hilālī and Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and the people of knowledge whom we have known have held it — is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be seen in the Hereafter with the eyes: the people of the Garden will see Him, but as for the rest of the children of Adam, they will not. He said: the proof for this is the ḥadīths transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ, that it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" — and he mentioned the ḥadīth. Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: and belief in these ḥadīths transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — on seeing the Lord at the Resurrection; on the decree; intercession; the punishment of the grave; the Basin; the Balance; the Dajjāl; stoning; the descent of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, every night after the half or the remaining third; the reckoning; the Fire and the Garden — that both are created and do not pass away; and that there is no one but Allah will speak to him on the Day of Resurrection with no interpreter between Him and him to interpret for him; and similar ḥadīths — and affirming them is binding upon the servants: they must believe in them, even if their minds do not reach them and they do not know their explanation. They must believe in them and submit, without [asking] how, without aversion «[Translator's note: «تنفير» in the source; perhaps «تفسير», "interpretation".]» and without analogy, because the acts of Allah are not likened to the acts of the servants.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the speech of the scholars known for [adherence to] the Sunna in every age, until it reached Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Jarīr. He mentioned the words of those who deny the vision, their argumentation and their sophistry, refuted that and made it clear; and we will mention his words verbatim, since he achieved in it what was intended, if Allah wills. He mentioned their objection from His saying, Exalted is He: لا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصارَ [al-Anʿām: 103]. As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic: قالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِي أَنْظُرْ إِلَيْكَ قالَ لَنْ تَرانِي [al-Aʿrāf: 143], it is something that needs no argument, because it contains evidence for the looking: since Mūsā ﷺ, with his rank, could not ask for what cannot be, this shows that it is possible for it to be; and the time at which he asked it was in this world, so the answer is that no one sees Him in this world. And he argued against their sophistry concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, لا تدركه الأبصار, with the statement of ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī on the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ناضِرَةٌ إِلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ — he said: they will look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic; their sight will not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them; and that is His saying: لا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصارُ. He said: those who hold this view argued from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: حَتَّى إِذا أَدْرَكَهُ الْغَرَقُ [Yūnus: 90] — and drowning is not described as having seen him. They said: so the meaning of «لا تدركه الأبصار» is far from the meaning of "they do not see Him", because a thing may overtake (يدرك) a thing without seeing it, as in «حتّى إذا أدركه الغرق»; and likewise a thing may see a thing without overtaking it. Similar is: قالَ أَصْحابُ مُوسى إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 61] — Pharaoh's people had seen them but had not overtaken them. And He, exalted be His praise, said: لا تَخافُ دَرَكاً [Ṭā Hā: 77]. So since a thing may see a thing without overtaking it, and overtake it without seeing it, it is known that «لا تدركه الأبصار» is far removed from the meaning "eyes do not see Him", and that its meaning is "eyes do not encompass Him", because encompassing Him is not possible. The believers and the people of the Garden will see their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, yet their eyes will not "overtake" Him, in the sense that they will not encompass Him, since it is not permissible to describe Allah as being encompassed by anything. Parallel to the permissibility of describing Him as being seen but not encompassed is the permissibility of describing Him as being known but not encompassed. He, Blessed and Exalted, said: وَلا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِما شاءَ [al-Baqara: 255]; the meaning of العلم here is "what is known". So His denying that His creatures encompass anything of His knowledge, except what He wills, was not a denial that they know it; it is only a denial of encompassing it. Likewise, in denying that sight overtakes Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when it sees Him, there is no denial of its seeing Him. Just as it is possible for creatures to know something without encompassing it in knowledge, so it is possible for them to see their Lord with their eyes without their eyes "overtaking" Him, since the meaning of seeing is other than the meaning of overtaking, and the meaning of overtaking is other than the meaning of seeing, because the meaning of overtaking is encompassing, as Ibn ʿAbbās said: eyes do not encompass Him, and He encompasses them. If it is said: "And why do you reject that the meaning of «لا تدركه الأبصار» is 'they do not see Him'?" we say to him: we reject that because Allah informed in His Book that faces at the Resurrection will be looking at Allah, glory be to Him, and the Prophet ﷺ informed that they will see their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection as they see the moon on the night it is full and as they see the sun with no cloud before it. The Book of Allah confirms itself, part by part; so it is known that the meaning of لا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصارُ is other than the meaning of إِلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ. He said: and it has been said: the meaning is that the eyes of creatures do not perceive Him in this world but will perceive Him in the Hereafter — so they made this specific. He said: and it has been said:
The meaning is that the eyes of the wrongdoers do not perceive Him in this world or the Hereafter, while the eyes of the believers perceive Him. And it has been said: «لا تدركه الأبصار» [means] by reaching the limit and encompassing; as for seeing — yes. And it has been said: eyes do not perceive Him as He perceives creatures, because their eyes are weak. Others said: the verse is general, and the sight of no one will ever perceive Allah, exalted be His praise, in this world or the Hereafter; but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will create for His friends on the Day of Resurrection a sixth sense besides their five senses, and they will see Him with it. The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what the reports from the Prophet ﷺ concur on: "You will see your Lord" — so the believers will see Him, and the unbelievers on that day will be veiled. The people of this doctrine have things with which they cause confusion: some of them reject the ḥadīth out of obstinacy and to attack the people of Islam, and some of them bring things that we dislike to mention. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: we have only mentioned this so that whoever looks into what we mean «[Translator's note: «نعني» in the source; perhaps «في كتابنا».]» may know that they fall back in their doctrine only on what Satan has confused for them, whose corruption the people of truth can easily expose; they do not fall back in their doctrine on any verse of the revelation, nor on any report from the Messenger, sound or weak. So they stumble about in darkness and wander in blindness. We seek refuge with Allah from bewilderment and misguidance. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the explanation of «تضارون» and the variation in its transmission, we will dictate it. There are eight forms in it: it is transmitted «تضارون» with a light [rāʾ] and «تضامون» with a light [mīm]; and تضامّون and تضارّون «[Translator's note: the source repeats «تضامّون» twice here; the second is evidently تضارّون.]» are permissible with ḍamma on the tāʾ and a doubled mīm and rāʾ; and تضامّون is permissible on the basis that the original is تتضامّون, with a tāʾ dropped, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا [Āl ʿImrān: 103]; and تضّامّون is permissible, assimilating the tāʾ into the ḍād; and تضارّون is permissible, with the tāʾ dropped; and تضّارّون is permissible, assimilating the tāʾ into the ḍād. What the meticulous transmitters have related is the light form: تضامون and تضارون. I heard Abū Isḥāq say: its meaning is "no injustice (ضيم) and no harm (ضير) will befall you in seeing Him", i.e. you will see Him so that you are all equal in seeing, and none of you will wrong another, nor will any of you harm another. The lexicographers gave two other views. They said: لا تضارّون with a doubled rāʾ and لا تضامّون with a doubled mīm, with ḍamma on the tāʾ; and some of them said: with fatḥa on the tāʾ and a doubled rāʾ and mīm, in the sense of تتضامّون and تتضارّون. The meaning of this is that none of you will contend with another, i.e. none of you will disagree with another in that. One says ضاررت فلانا أضارّه مضارّة وضرارا, when you disagree with him. And the meaning of لا تضامّون في رؤيته is that none of you will press up to another, one saying to the other "Show Him to me", as they do when looking for the new moon.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what we mentioned of al-Aʿmash's explanation, that its meaning is لا تضارّون [you will not dispute], requires that his transmission be لا تضارّون, the original being لا تضاررون «[Translator's note: the source has «لا تضارون»; the unassimilated form تضاررون is evidently meant.]», with the rāʾ then assimilated into the rāʾ. And whoever says its meaning is لا تضارّون, the original in his view is لا تضارون «[Translator's note: again, تضاررون is evidently meant.]», then assimilated. All of this is from ضارّه, when he disagrees with him, as Abū Isḥāq reported — "he disagreed with him and the two did not share one view" «[Translator's note: the source has «وخالفه وما رآه واحد», which seems corrupt; translated tentatively.]». And one says: نضر وجهه, نضرا, نضارة and نضرة; and نضره الله ينضره and أنضره ينضره, from radiance, bliss, a good life and wealth.
